doc.title: Dorothy Donegan — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Retirement, popularity cycles and benefit performances
summary: Marriage and children retired her for a while; she regained popularity by playing for Delores Hope and benefits that awaken promoters.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: How about between marriages and having two sons, did you ever retire from the business?
No, it retired me for a while. This is a funny business. One day you’re Jay bird and the next day, the same day, you’re Jay Gould.
Have you found that to be true in that order, going from lacking popularity to becoming popular again? What would lead to those new peaks in popularity for you?
Well, in Chicago I had unpopularity, but I played for Delores Hope and we got a standing ovation, so I got popular again there. You can do a benefit sometimes and it awakens the promoters.
